One of the fundamental biological processes that occurs in living organisms is the breakdown of food into smaller components that can be used by the body for energy and growth. This process is called cellular respiration.

The central idea of cellular respiration is that cells take in oxygen and glucose (a type of sugar found in food) and convert them into energy in the form of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), which cells can use to carry out their functions. The process also produces carbon dioxide and water as waste products.

The sequence of cellular respiration involves several steps:

1. Glycolysis: In this stage, glucose is broken down into two molecules of pyruvate in the cytoplasm of the cell. This process produces a small amount of ATP and some molecules called NADH, which will be used later in the process.
